scenario: [LINT.7.2]: a component read is an operation on the interval ([LINT.6.1]), so `.duration` of an invalid interval raises DOMAIN. One T with `a` at 2 s and `b` at 1 s, `b` before `a`: rule `no_length` tests `(s.a .. s.b).duration == 0_s`. It does not fire, and rule `handler` logs `DOMAIN [T] [a]`: the kind, and the schema and slot of the pair's start ([LERR.9.12]); not the `rule`, which for a trap raised during matching is a node name ([LERR.9.2]). Before RLOW.6.1.7 the lowering saturated `end - start` at `0_s`, so `no_length` fired silently; that is the break this vector is for. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `lint_6_1_component` wrapped in FN_INTERVAL_CHECK(s, e, v) by `rlow_6_1_7_check`, on `Time` endpoints compared by their `utc_ns` ([LTIM.5]), in libds `eval_interval_check` (rete/eval.c) and Mercury `ds.eval.rlow_6_1_7_interval_check`.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: Int key
    a: Time mutable
    b: Time mutable

rule no_length:
    T s where (s.a .. s.b).duration == 0_s
->
    log info "no_length {s.id}"

rule handler:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind} [{e.schema}] [{e.slot}]"
